the_model_on_the_same_held_out_set.method: the model in this session, given the 64-skill catalog and the 64 held-out requests, answers written to a file before any scoring
the_model_on_the_same_held_out_set.across_library_sizes: 100% at n=10, 25, 50 and 64 -- it does not degrade, because every skill is visible regardless of how many there are
the_model_on_the_same_held_out_set.prompt_cost: ~514 tokens for 64 skills = 8.0 tokens/skill; ~8,000 tokens at 1,000 skills -- inside a modern context

the_answer_to_the_original_question.is_a_learned_skill_library_a_solution_to: no, and the last four rounds have measured why, in order: it transfers only to a new INSTANCE of a taught task (r65); skills compose, which does compound (r66); a library is worth what can be FOUND in it, and findability collapses to 0/10 when the user does not speak library vocabulary (r67); and every cheap similarity measure decays as the library grows (r68-69)
the_answer_to_the_original_question.so_what_is_the_fast_correct_move: do not build a better thesaurus. SHOW THE MODEL THE CATALOG. It is exact on vocabulary it has never seen, it does not degrade with size, and the catalog costs 8 tokens per skill
the_answer_to_the_original_question.and_then: the library's value is not that it lets the agent skip the model. It is that it gives the model precise, executable, cause-checked actions to choose from instead of raw clicks

what_this_does_not_prove: one model, 64 requests, one catalog: not a benchmark
